source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Check SSD could be insert/remove

1. Insert SSD to BP.
2. Remove SSD form BP.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: 1. Make sure SSD could insert/remove normally.

original_test_intent: Verify by direct handling that each specified SSD can be inserted into and removed from the intended backplane bay normally, without abnormal resistance, latch/connector damage or unsafe service behavior; enumeration/log checks are supplemental when the operation is hot-plugged.
original_method: A qualified operator confirms the bay's powered-off or hot-swap procedure, maps the exact SSD serial and bay, performs the insertion and removal while judging mechanics and safe behavior, and records physical evidence; the agent may capture pre/post inventory, health and logs without controlling the bay.
manual_activity: Physical insertion/removal and tactile assessment of normal carrier, latch and connector behavior are the core stimulus and criterion. The agent can only collect supplemental enumeration/log evidence and cannot claim the physical cycle, so MANUAL ONLY applies rather than PARTIAL.
required_inputs: Exact SSD serial/model, carrier/tray, backplane and bay mapping
Platform service SOP stating hot-swap capability or required powered-off state
Mounted/in-use/RAID/OS/data membership and authorized data/workload disposition
Mechanical force/latch/seating criteria, cycle count if more than the single source cycle, and operator
Expected enumeration/log behavior if powered hot-plug evidence is required
safety_requirements: Never hot-remove a bay unless platform and storage policy explicitly support it and all affected data/workloads are protected.
Verify carrier orientation and bay identity; stop on resistance, stuck latch, connector damage, sparks, power fault or unexpected system/storage state.
Do not command bay power or write to the SSD as part of this mechanical case unless separately approved.
Preserve as-found and per-cycle evidence; do not auto-retry or repeat a suspect insertion/removal.
agent_execution_scope: Prepare the bay/serial/service-state checklist and read-only baseline inventory/log capture.
During operator action, capture approved pre/post device, health and kernel/BMC log evidence for the exact serial when applicable.
Organize the operator's physical observation and supplemental evidence as Tool Result without claiming execution or verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve the service state, target bay/drive, data impact and cycle scope.
Perform and attest the physical insert/remove and judge normal mechanics.
Resolve any mechanical or detection anomaly and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `lsblk` and `dmesg` can corroborate a powered hot-plug but cannot prove normal physical insertion/removal. A short dmesg tail can miss events and is unnecessary for a powered-off purely mechanical execution.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Retain operator physical execution. If hot-swap is approved, collect target-filtered, timestamped inventory and complete relevant kernel/BMC event ranges as supplemental evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: One explicit insert and remove, backplane target and 15/8-minute fields are preserved; no repeated cycle count is invented.

modernized_recommendation.status: MANUAL PHYSICAL CYCLE WITH TARGETED TELEMETRY
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a bay/serial-bound operator checklist and video/photo evidence, with optional event-triggered inventory, health and log capture only when the approved hot-swap procedure requires powered detection.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact SSD carrier/backplane/bay and service mode.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record chassis/backplane/controller/drive firmware, OS/kernel and inventory-tool versions where telemetry is used.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform backplane/hot-swap and storage service documentation must define safe handling.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds identity/data safety and traceable evidence without replacing the hands-on action.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; physical insert/remove normality remains the primary criterion.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Clean enumeration does not prove connector mechanics, and mechanical success does not automatically prove hot-plug data integrity.

project_override_considerations: A project may define powered-off versus hot-swap execution and additional cycle count. Claims must state the actual mode/count and may not infer hot-swap coverage from a powered-off mechanical check.
expected_evidence: SSD/carrier/backplane/bay identities, service-state/hot-swap authorization and operator identity
Operator-attributed insertion/removal photos/video and mechanical observations
If powered: exact serial pre/post enumeration, health and timestamped kernel/BMC events plus data/workload state
Any stop/anomaly, final safe state, Tool Result and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and criterion consistently require normal SSD insertion and removal. Hot-swap/detection telemetry is supplemental historical interpretation, not a conflicting source requirement.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The physical operation is clear. Missing service-mode or mapping inputs are readiness conditions; the hands-on core is MANUAL ONLY.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retains its useful read-only telemetry but corrects PARTIAL because the source's primary test is physical handling.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains hot-swap, mapping and data-integrity safeguards while applying MANUAL ONLY under the locked physical-core rule.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates powered hot-plug evidence from powered-off mechanical coverage and preserves the source's single-cycle count.

review_improvement: Prevents remote enumeration from being claimed as a physical plug test and protects live storage through explicit service-state and data checks.
independent_technical_reasoning: The named and accepted action is to insert and remove the SSD normally. That physical operation cannot be delegated to an agent or proven by software, so the whole case is MANUAL ONLY even though automated telemetry can assist.
